merge_reason: Kept separate: this is an indication, comparative-therapy, guideline and deprescribing audit for edema and lipedema, requiring a broad clinical/regulatory evidence set.
prompt: Required researcher: prochatgpt_researcher. Audit the clinical and regulatory question: when a person with lipedema also has edema or another condition, when do diuretics have a real indication and when is there little or no benefit? Compare loop, thiazide/thiazide-like, mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonist and other potassium-sparing agents, acetazolamide, and SGLT2 inhibitors that patients may call water pills. Separate pure lipedema, venous/lymphatic edema, idiopathic/orthostatic edema, heart failure, kidney disease, cirrhosis and hypertension. Review current ESC/AHA/KDIGO/EASL/AEMPS/EMA/ISL/S2k guidance, systematic reviews and trials, deprescribing/withdrawal evidence, rebound versus recurrence of the underlying condition, neurohormonal adaptation, monitoring and urgent signs. Explicitly verify whether any lipedema-specific diuretic trial exists. Open primary pages/PMIDs/DOIs and Spanish/European product information; do not use snippets, SEO clinics, supplements or marketing as evidence. Return a source table, dates, evidence class, population, limitations, contradictions, safe plain-language Spanish wording and a falsation pass against “diuretics always worsen lipedema,” “MRA/SGLT2 are only water loss,” and “all post-withdrawal swelling is rebound.” Mark blocked/partial/failed sources and uncertainty.
